column3: The edit identifies scanner reading versus the owner's reported number. The gloss mistranslates the chip as a crystal.
The paired edit isolates the path above versus below the wall. The gloss adds an unsupported wall material.
The gloss exposes the reversed sequence but misidentifies both the strip and the insert, obscuring which actions are sequenced.
The gloss misidentifies a wrinkled sample and mistranslates the exception, even though it retains the routing to the clean-sample procedure.
A thin layer corresponds to the one-coat Chinese instruction, in contrast to two coats in English.
The local edit isolates the first-versus-second profile selection.
The gloss retains first rather than second whistle, but wrongly describes water coming down instead of telling participants when to enter.
The gloss preserves export being limited to records without personal data instead of suppressing only their notes.
The only Chinese content is the easy-grip cup instruction and the table-number step is absent.
The gloss makes the stage supervisor confirm a pre-modified script, losing the receipt-versus-revision sequence.
The gloss gives yellow instead of blue. It also garbles the redemption exception that both originals share.
The comparison identifies posting to the class feed versus keeping the recording in an individual portfolio.
The gloss drops the Chinese no-permission requirement and falsely claims written permission is needed.
The warning focuses on the agreed drum-cover instruction and fails to identify the inventory-section mismatch.
The gloss exposes before versus after but mistranslates the insert as a cabinet and the adhesive strip as a ribbon.
The gloss describes black underwear instead of black-soled shoes and therefore supplies the wrong object of the permission contrast.
The edits expose an outward pull versus an inward press, despite the gloss's rendering of the trolley handle as the driver's handle.
The gloss keeps reception as the required location, but mistranslates overshoes as ordinary shoes.
